_description: One row per process-state transition observed within a case. Transitions are derived from sequential filing events. A single company case generates 2–8 transitions across its lifecycle. This table calibrates sequence quality and state-change probabilities.

triggering_event_id.description: Foreign key to filing_events.csv — the filing that caused this transition.

transition_date.description: Date of the filing that caused the transition. Same as triggering_event filing_date.

transition_type.description: Matches transition event types from process_history.py for cross-system compatibility.

sequence_type.description: Compound sequence pattern active at this transition. Derived from filing history up to transition_date only (no look-ahead).

sequence_window_days.description: Days spanned by the compound sequence (time from first signal to this transition). 0 if no compound sequence.

compound_signal_quality.description: Compound quality label at this transition. Matches sequence_detector.py CQ labels.

supporting_events.description: Pipe-separated list of event_ids that contributed to this compound sequence.

days_since_prior_transition.description: Calendar days since the previous transition in this case.

days_since_case_start.description: Calendar days from case first_observation_date to this transition.

interpretation.description: Rule-based interpretation of this transition. What it means strategically, based only on information available at transition_date.

eventual_outcome.description: What ultimately happened to this case. Filled in retrospectively once outcome is known. Do NOT fill during initial labeling — this is outcome data, not signal data.

days_transition_to_outcome.description: Calendar days from this specific transition to final outcome resolution. Useful for calibrating time-to-outcome from different process states.

verified.description: True if transition dates, filing URLs, and state labels confirmed against primary EDGAR source.
